chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Abu Baseer, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'A man dies and leaves dependents. Are they given from the Zakat?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Yes, until they grow up and reach adulthood, and can ask, from where would they be living when that is cut off from them.' So I said, 'They do not know (the Wilayah/Religion).' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Their deceased [father] should be preserved among them, and the Religion of their father should be made beloved to them, so they will not long before they pay attention to their father's Religion. So when they reach adulthood and turn to others, then do not give to them.'
ai.seo_question: Can Zakat be given to the young children of a deceased believer for their upbringing?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies that Zakat can be used to support the young dependents of a deceased believer until they reach maturity, emphasizing the preservation of their religious identity through the father's legacy. The condition for continued support is their adherence to the father's faith; if they deviate or 'turn to others' (often interpreted as other sects or schools of thought), the entitlement ceases, reflecting the Shia emphasis on religious continuity alongside material sustenance.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Hareyz, from Abu Baseer who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘A man dies and leave the dependants. Would they be given from the Zakāt?’ Heasws said: ‘Yes, until they grow up and reach adulthood, and can asked, from where would they be living when that is cut off from them’. So I said, ‘They are not recognising (Al-Wilayah)’. Heasws said: ‘Their deceased should be preserved among them, and the Religion of their father should be made to be beloved to them, it won’t be long before they pay attention to their Religion. So when reach adulthood and change to others, then do not give to them’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Hariz from abu Basir who has said the following: “

I once asked abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who dies and leaves behind dependents. Can Zakat be given to them? He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, until they grow up, become adults and ask (themselves) by what means could they live and survive if that Zakat was cut off from them. I then said, ‘They do not know. He (the Imam) said, ‘The memories of their dead must be preserved and the religion of their father must be made beloved to them, so that they pay attention to the religion of their father; and if they become adults and decide to go to others; then do not give them any Zakat.”
